title: Combination Sum
statement: Candidates are distinct positive integers. Return all unique combinations that add up to the target, where the same candidate may be used any number of times. Order does not matter.

hints.1_question: Each candidate can be used repeatedly. How do you let a number be chosen again but still avoid producing the same combination in a different order?
hints.2_nudge: Recurse with a `start` index: after choosing candidates[i], continue from i (not i + 1) so it can repeat, but never go back to earlier indices.
hints.3_big_hint: bt(start, rem): if rem == 0 record; for i from start: if cands[i] > rem break; append; bt(i, rem - cands[i]); pop.

known_bugs.name: each candidate used at most once
known_bugs.followup: The same number may be used many times. After choosing index i, which index should the next call start from?

known_bugs.name: restarts from index 0 (same combo in many orders)
stops after the first solution
known_bugs.followup: The task asks for ALL combinations. How many does your function return for [2,3,6,7] and 7?

followups: Why does sorting allow an early break?
How would a DP over the target compare for just counting combinations?
